prompt_policy.generation: No GPT-4/API request was made. The English candidate text below was supplied in the Experiment 41 task and frozen after source/mapping review.
prompt_policy.role: Literature metadata organizes candidate anatomical evidence; it is not an individual diagnosis or connection-level ground truth.
prompt_policy.text_encoder: None. Natural-language text is not embedded or freely projected. Model use is restricted to frozen, auditable ROI/edge masks and direction-uncertainty metadata.
prompt_policy.freeze_rule: Prompt text, source metadata and masks are frozen before training. Test-fold results cannot change them.

concepts.prompt_text: At the group level, autistic participants may show increased convergence of negative functional connectivity deviations involving sensorimotor and attention-associated regions. This is a network- or region-level population observation, not a universal reduction in any individual ROI-to-ROI connection.
concepts.source_title: Ilioska et al., Nature Mental Health (2026)
concepts.evidence_scale: region/network; not a fixed individual edge
concepts.supported_direction: negative at population regional-convergence scale only; individual signs remain free
concepts.direction_uncertainty: high; do not impose an edge sign
concepts.provenance: Candidate wording supplied by the user; ROI names are exact-name matches against the audited Harvard-Oxford ROI table. Edges require both verified endpoints to be in the candidate set.

concepts.concept_name: Insular, temporal and prefrontal regional deviations
concepts.prompt_text: Atypical connectivity deviations may converge on insular, temporal, and prefrontal regions in subsets of autistic individuals. The existence and direction of deviation for a particular subject must be determined from measured connectivity relative to a suitable normative reference, not from the anatomical name alone.
concepts.source_title: Ilioska et al., Nature Mental Health (2026)
concepts.direction_uncertainty: high; preserve positive and negative channels
concepts.provenance: Candidate wording supplied by the user; conservative HO name matching only. Edges require both verified endpoints to be in the candidate set.

concepts.concept_name: Medial prefrontal, cingulate and inferior-parietal positive deviations
concepts.prompt_text: Positive normative connectivity deviations have shown increased regional convergence involving medial prefrontal, cingulate and inferior parietal areas in autism research. This population-scale finding should not be translated into a mandatory positive sign for individual observed edges.
concepts.source_title: Ilioska et al., Nature Mental Health (2026)
concepts.evidence_scale: regional; not a fixed individual edge
concepts.supported_direction: positive at population regional-convergence scale only; individual signs remain free
concepts.direction_uncertainty: high; do not impose an edge sign
concepts.provenance: Candidate wording supplied by the user; exact HO atlas names are used where present. Edges require both verified endpoints to be in the candidate set.

concepts.prompt_text: Some autistic populations show convergent positive deviations involving default-mode and cognitive-control systems. Apply this concept only if the current ROI-to-system correspondence is independently verified; otherwise retain the concept as literature metadata without asserting precise network membership.
concepts.source_title: Ilioska et al., Nature Mental Health (2026)
not_supported_claims: precise ROI membership in this dataset
concepts.provenance: Retained as metadata only because the selected 111-column HO set has no independently verified canonical functional-network assignment.

concepts.prompt_text: Negative connectivity deviations have been reported across some somatomotor and associative system relationships. These findings are heterogeneous and depend on network definition, age, preprocessing and sampling; anatomical name similarity alone is insufficient to assign an observed connection to a canonical network.
concepts.source_title: Ilioska et al., Nature Mental Health (2026)
concepts.provenance: Retained as metadata only; no canonical network mapping is inferred from broad atlas labels.

concepts.prompt_text: Atypical subcortical and cortical connectivity may contribute to distributed brain-system differences in autism. The candidate should preserve uncertainty in direction and acknowledge that the current sparse selected-connectivity set may provide incomplete evidence for the underlying system.
concepts.source_title: Ilioska et al., Nature Mental Health (2026); Kobbersmed et al., Progress in Neurobiology (2026)
concepts.provenance: Only verified selected FCs with exactly one HO subcortical and one cortical endpoint are eligible. The 252-edge RFE subset is incomplete.

concepts.prompt_text: No reliable disease-specific semantic correspondence can be asserted for this observed deviation when anatomical coverage, normative reference support, measurement reliability or direct literature support is insufficient. Preserve the observed numeric information without forcing it to match an ASD-related concept.
concepts.provenance: Reject mass is calculated from training-TD-calibrated evidence strength, reference support and anatomical coverage; it is not a disease probability.
